label: Content-fixed favouring explains a contrast: the actual content favours the outcome over the rival
definition: FavouringExplains fav e h out y is fav (e h) (out h) y: the content e h that an explanatory level supplies at history h counts in favour of the actual outcome out h over y. OutcomeIndependent e: e is the same at every compared history, so the content is fixed independently of which outcome occurs. FavouringSelects: the content favours the actual outcome over every other realized outcome. Favouring does not exclude y from the level's choice cell. Law 1 of FavouringStandardLaws assumes each content's favouring is asymmetric (net favouring); a content with pro tanto reasons in both directions is outside that law's scope.
note: Stipulated to give a contrastive standard on which the explanans is individuated independently of the outcome partition (#2145, Lane 2b). It is the cell-carrier analogue of net favouring (SELECTING_AN_OUTCOME_1, NetSelects, DEF 7e29ff7f), not one of its senses and not bridged to it. Unlike the determination standard (DEF 5a818c39), a bare re-description of the outcome is excluded by the admission condition (outcome independence); law 1 adds that no outcome-independent asymmetric content selects whatever outcome occurs (the #742 core on cells). Law 1 excludes every profile of the good-favouring table equally and so does not itself discriminate among them. See docs/notes/optimal-creation-choice.md §§65–69.
